claims.text: The proposed computational method will incorporate machine-learning potentials.
The proposed method can accurately predict lattice and electronic heat-transport contributions in HfNbTaTiZr.
Separate models will be used for the lattice and electronic contributions.
The method will reduce mean absolute error by at least 15% relative to earlier approaches.
The method will account for atomic-scale complexity, including defects and impurities such as oxygen.
The relevant initial material is bulk refractory HfNbTaTiZr that may contain defects or impurities, including approximately 1 wt.% oxygen.
Machine-learning potentials reduce the computational cost of first-principles heat-transport simulations.
Machine-learning potentials increase the precision of simulations of lattice and electronic heat transport.
Accounting for defects and impurities will enable more accurate separation and prediction of lattice and electronic heat-transport contributions.
At 300 K, the lattice thermal-conductivity contribution is predicted to be 5–10 W/(K m).
At 300 K, the electronic thermal-conductivity contribution is predicted to be 5–7 W/(K m).
Earlier measurements reported total thermal conductivity of 10–17 W/(K m) from 300 to 1200 K.
The proposed method is applicable below 200 K and from 300 to 1200 K for bulk crystals with potentially varying defect or impurity concentrations.
Prediction accuracy may depend on training-data quality and material-system complexity.
The method may fail to capture all relevant atomic-scale complexity.
The hypothesis is falsified if mean absolute error is not reduced by at least 15% relative to earlier approaches or if predictions differ from experiment by more than 10%.
